title: Provenance Layer: Rapid Reading Notes and To-Dos
content:
Purpose: quick consolidated brain dump after the provenance/traceability session at the internal reading group. Not polished — for my own followups and to share with Mira/Ibrahim for prioritization.

Top-level takeaways (TLDR):
- Provenance as a lightweight middleware layer is useful for: debugging reranked outputs, audit trails for enterprise, and targeted evals for drift.
- Distinguish three operational tiers: 1) token-level traces (costly, rare), 2) segment-level provenance (KV hits, retrieval IDs), 3) session-level metadata (model variant, rollout id, routing path).
- For inference economics, we should default to segment-level provenance + probabilistic sampling of token-level traces (heuristic triggers).

Papers / posts skimmed (quick notes):
1) 'Lightweight Provenance for Neural Retrieval' (arXiv 2029) — core idea: store compressed retrieval signatures and a small stable fingerprint for each retrieved chunk.
  Notes: fingerprinting via locality-sensitive hashing (LSH) then delta-compress storage; fast lookup for FAQ-like queries. They show 6x reduction in storage vs naive URIs and ~0.8 accuracy for attribution tasks.
  Implication: pair LSH fingerprint with our existing KV-cache keys (we already have hash keys per chunk) — stores cheaply in Redis + S3 cold archive.

2) 'Shotgun Tracing: Probabilistic Token Traces for Production' (conference workshop slide deck) — idea to avoid full token logs by sampling tokens at points of high surprise and storing context windows around those tokens.
  Notes: interesting trigger functions (next-token perplexity > tau, user-reported 'wrong' signal). Their sampling approach saved 90% logging cost while capturing 85% of failure modes in their eval.

3) Engineering blog: 'Practical Audit Trails for Chatbots' — pragmatic checklist (consent, retention policies, redaction, KMS).
  Notes: important legal/compliance constraints. For Private deployments we need default redaction hooks (PII scrub) before archiving provenance. Add this as a product requirement.

Rough sketches and heuristics I care about:
- Provenance envelope schema (minimal): {session_id, model_id, model_variant, route, retrieval_ids[], kv_cache_hits[], trace_mode_flag, event_time, debug_bucket}.
  - Keep schema minimal in the hot path. Only expand when trace_mode_flag==ON.
- Trace_mode heuristics: on for canary users, on after semantic-similarity regression triggers, on user-complaint endpoint.
- Sampling policy: base sample rate r0=0.01 for token traces, boost to r1=0.2 for requests where reranker changed top-1 candidate, or where perplexity spike observed.

Planned experiments (short-term):
1) 'KV-provenance smoke': instrument a staging stack to emit KV-cache hit IDs for 1% of requests. Measure: additional payload size, Redis throughput, and how often KV hits correlate with stable outputs (test corpora). Owner: me. Target: 2 weeks.
2) 'Surprise-triggered trace': integrate simple perplexity trigger (lightweight approx using small LM) to sample token windows. Compare coverage of human-labeled failures vs random sampling. Owner: Ibrahim. Target: 3 weeks.
3) 'Retention & redaction baseline': prototype redaction step before archival for Private deployments. Try redaction via regex+NER flagging; measure false positives on downstream evals. Owner: Mira. Target: 4 weeks.

Open questions / risks (notes to self):
- Storage cost vs debug value: what's the marginal benefit per GB of traces? Need to propose an internal ROI approach (match debug fix rate to samples).
- Privacy & consent surface for hosted API customers — we can offer provenance toggles per-tenant, but is that too granular? Need legal input.
- Latency add: synchronous provenance writes may add p99. Must be async or best-effort.
- Security: provenance may leak PII; redaction must be robust, but redaction can remove signals needed for debugging. Consider dual-store: redacted hot store + encrypted cold store for legal review.

Concrete next steps (my sprint todo):
- Create PR skeleton to emit KV hit IDs (redis key + chunk id) in the request trace envelope. Link to GH draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/prov-experiments/pull/57 (WIP).
- Draft a short Confluence page describing provenance levels + retention options for product review (link placeholder CONFLUENCE-PLAT-1423).
- Schedule 30-min sync with Mira/Ibrahim next Tue to assign tasks and pick sampling thresholds.

Random micro-ideas (seed for future):
- 'Attribution probes': synthetic prompt set where we know which chunk should be responsible for answer; useful for measuring provenance sharpness.
- 'Provenance-aware reranker': reranker that takes retrieval signature features + provenance freshness to reweight candidates. Could help degrade gracefully when cold cache.

Notes-to-self (short):
- Keep provenance payload under 256B by default (use compact ids).
- Avoid token-level trace by default — it's too costly.
- Coordinate with security early for KMS/encryption decisions.

---
Session log: quick timeline of how this doc evolved:
- 2029-06-21: reading group + first draft notes (created).
- 2029-06-23: added experiment plan after chat with Ibrahim.
- 2029-06-25: redaction / legal considerations added.

If you read this and want to co-own any experiment, ping me (daniela@redwood) or drop a comment on the GH draft.

End of notes.
